Counterpoint Research published its latest research report predicting that consumer wearable devices will accumulate over US$1 trillion in revenue by 2032, led by smartwatches and wireless earbuds. Details below.

Smartwatches and wireless earbuds are expected to dominate the market

A report published today by Counterpoint Research points out that "the global consumer wearable device market is expected to generate over US$1 trillion in total revenue between 2026 and 2032."

The report categorises consumer wearable devices and predicts that hearables will account for the largest share of accumulated revenue, at approximately US$360 billion, followed by smartwatches at US$304 billion, and smart glasses at US$168 billion.

Report contents:

Health patches are expected to generate an additional US$120 billion in revenue, followed by smart rings at US$44 billion, neck-worn devices at US$24 billion, smart shoes at US$18 billion, and fitness bands at US$14 billion. As for smart socks, smart clothing, and smart belts, each category is expected to generate less than US$10 billion in revenue.

Counterpoint Research points out that the revenue growth rate of consumer wearable devices is twice the shipment growth rate, and more notably, the market appears to be gradually shifting from health data tracking to preventive healthcare, "that is, devices alert users before they notice anything abnormal."

As for Apple, it competes in two of the categories with the highest expected revenue — namely AirPods and Apple Watch. Apple is reportedly also developing smart glasses, and there are also rumours that the company is exploring screen-less fitness bands and smart rings.

Apple disclosed last month that its "Wearables, Home and Accessories" category recorded US$7.88 billion in revenue in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026, a year-on-year increase of 6%, marking the strongest growth for this category since the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2022.

Although this category is clearly not just about wearables, Apple has been actively expanding this area for many years, viewing it as an important revenue source. Counterpoint expects that AirPods alone will surpass US$100 billion in accumulated revenue in 2026.
